persistent_identifier_status: Repository-local stable transcription identifier; article DOI is the persistent source identifier.
title: Second-year grass response and soil nutrient status after De Marke biorefinery struvite application
citation: Szymańska, M., Sosulski, T., Bożętka, A., Dawidowicz, U., Wąs, A., Szara, E., Malak-Rawlikowska, A., Sulewski, P., van Pruissen, G. W. P., & Cornelissen, R. L. (2020). Evaluating the Struvite Recovered from Anaerobic Digestate in a Farm Bio-Refinery as a Slow-Release Fertiliser. Energies, 13(20), 5342. https://doi.org/10.3390/en13205342
geography: Struvite produced from cattle-slurry digestate at De Marke farm biorefinery, Hengelo (Gld), Netherlands; greenhouse pot experiment conducted in Warsaw, Poland using silty loam from Obory and loamy sand from Skierniewice.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), as stated in the published article footer.
material_scope: Second-year grass and soil response after one-time application of fine recovered struvite, struvite supplemented with ammonium sulphate, or commercial ammonium phosphate. Struvite originated from the liquid fraction of anaerobically digested cattle slurry at a Dutch farm biorefinery.
experimental_conditions: Greenhouse pot study established in 2017, with three replicates and two soils (silty loam and loamy sand). Fertiliser was applied in May 2017; no fertiliser was applied in 2018. Lolium multiflorum was harvested four times during the second growing period. Plant nutrients were measured on above-ground dry matter; soil chemistry was assessed after harvest. The article reports struvite particle linear dimension of approximately 1400 µm and cautions that results may not represent commercial granules.
data_scope: 185 records: 12 Table 1 nutrient-dose records; 96 Table 2 plant N/P/Mg concentrations by treatment, soil and harvest; 12 Table 3 relative fertiliser-efficiency records; 48 Table 4 soil-property records; 8 narrative crop-yield means or pooled treatment means; and 9 explicit narrative nutrient-uptake values. Table 2 and Table 4 significance labels are transcribed. Table 3 efficiency values are source-calculated. Yield and uptake values whose uncertainty is only plotted were not digitized.
source_locations: Table 1, article p. 3: applied nutrient doses
Table 2, article p. 7: grass N/P/Mg concentrations by four 2018 harvests
Table 3, article p. 10: source-calculated relative fertiliser efficiency
Table 4, article p. 11: soil pH, total N, active/available P and active/available Mg
Results 3.1, article p. 5: explicit cumulative and pooled second-year yield means
Results 3.3, article pp. 8-9: explicit nutrient uptake values; figures not digitized
limitations: All records are reference-only. Cattle-slurry-derived struvite and Polish greenhouse soils are not roadside-grass-derived product or Dutch field validation.
No fertiliser was applied in the second growing year. Results represent residual response after 2017 application, not an annual application response.
The experiment has three pot replicates per treatment; it is not a replicated field trial.
Table 2 and Table 4 do not provide numeric standard deviations in the tables; significance letters and ns labels are retained, and blank SD cells are not zero.

Yield and nutrient-uptake uncertainty is shown graphically but was not digitized. Numeric means explicitly stated in article text are transcribed; pooled group means are not split into treatment values.
Relative fertiliser efficiency is a ratio of control-corrected nutrient uptake against ammonium phosphate, not nutrient recovery from digestate or a fertilizer substitution factor.
The source discusses fine struvite crystals of approximately 1400 µm and cautions against direct transfer to commercial granules; product particle size and use conditions matter.
No nutrient credit, product revenue, GreenHub default, model parameter or runtime calculation consumes this dataset.
conversion_or_processing: Transcribed numeric table cells and explicitly stated narrative values with original treatment, soil, harvest, unit and basis. The source equation for relative fertiliser efficiency is documented in record notes. No conversion, statistical inference, figure digitization, midpoint estimation or treatment disaggregation was performed.
uncertainty: Replicate count n=3 is reported by the source. Numeric SD is absent from Tables 2-4 and not extracted from figures. Statistical group letters are preserved where reported. Uncertainty is not imputed.
